paragraphs: Friend, this is a heavy one, and I won't pretend otherwise. The LORD tells Moses, "Take vengeance on the Midianites for the Israelites," and Moses calls it "the LORD's vengeance" (Numbers 31:2-3). The walkthrough reminded us that the LORD said the Midianites had deceived Israel in the matter of Peor (Numbers 25:16-18). So the big idea starts here: the LORD takes sin against His people seriously, and He is the One who answers it, not people on their own say-so.

Now look at what happens after the battle. Moses is angry with the officers, and the army still has to stay outside the camp for seven days to be purified (Numbers 31:14, 19). Then the commanders count their soldiers and say, "not one of us is missing," and they bring gold "to make atonement for ourselves before the LORD" (Numbers 31:49-50). I think they knew that even after a battle the LORD commanded, they could not just walk back into camp like nothing happened. Holiness is real, and coming near to God takes cleansing.

Here's what I carry from this, baker. Nobody walks into God's presence on their own record, and the people in this chapter knew it, so they brought an offering and waited to be made clean. I know what it's like to be dusty and worn out, and I know it takes Someone else to make a stamper new. Keep your ovens ready, friend, and come to the LORD humble, because He is the One who cleans us up.
